test_title: SSC CHSL 2025 Tier-1 (Held On: 28 Nov, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: In January 2025, which of the following is NOT among the six cities where the Supreme Court of India banned manual scavenging?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jaipur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Supreme Court of India** in January 2025 reinforced the ban on **manual scavenging** in six major cities of India, highlighting the inhumane and illegal nature of the practice.
 
• The six cities where manual scavenging was specifically banned include **Delhi, Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad, Kolkata, and Mumbai**.
 
• **Jaipur** is **not** among the six cities listed by the Supreme Court where the ban was enforced, making it the correct answer.
 
• This decision is part of India's ongoing efforts to uphold human dignity, ensure sanitation workers' rights, and enforce the **Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013**.
 
• Despite the ban, challenges in implementation persist across India, with reports of violations and inadequate rehabilitation measures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Manual Scavenging:**

 
 
• Manual scavenging refers to the practice of manually cleaning, carrying, or disposing of human excreta from dry latrines, open drains, or sewers.
 
• This practice is predominantly carried out by individuals from marginalized communities, often leading to severe social discrimination and health hazards.
 
 
 
• **Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013:**
 
 
• This Act prohibits the employment of manual scavengers and mandates the demolition of insanitary latrines.
 
• It also outlines measures for the rehabilitation of individuals engaged in manual scavenging, including alternative employment opportunities.
 
 
 
• **Supreme Court's Role:**
 
 
• The Supreme Court has consistently emphasized the eradication of manual scavenging, terming it a violation of fundamental rights under **Article 21** (Right to Life).
 
• The Court has directed governments to ensure proper implementation of the 2013 Act, along with compensation and rehabilitation for affected individuals.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Eradication:**
 
 
• Despite legal prohibitions, manual scavenging persists due to socio-economic factors, lack of enforcement, and inadequate sanitation infrastructure.
 
• The absence of mechanized cleaning equipment in many areas exacerbates the issue.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Government Initiatives:**

 
 
• The **Swachh Bharat Mission** was launched in 2014 to eliminate open defecation and promote sanitation infrastructure, reducing the need for manual scavenging.
 
• Various state governments have introduced schemes to rehabilitate manual scavengers by providing skill training, financial support, and alternative employment.
 
 
 
• **Data and Statistics:**
 
 
• According to a 2020 report by the **National Commission for Safai Karamcharis**, over 66,000 manual scavengers were identified across India, despite the legal ban.
 
• The majority of manual scavengers belong to the **Scheduled Castes**, highlighting the deep-rooted caste-based discrimination associated with the practice.
